📚 Today you learned

Moving Averages (50-day / 200-day) as Institutional Support

The 50-day and 200-day simple moving averages aren't magic — they're just the average closing price over that window. Their power comes from being widely watched: enough institutional capital treats a bounce off the 200-day as a "buy the trend" signal that it becomes somewhat self-fulfilling. A stock trading above both, with the 50-day above the 200-day (a "golden cross" structure), is in a confirmed uptrend. IQV right now: price is well above both its 50-day ($171.64) and 200-day ($195.75) after the late-July breakout — that's healthy structure, not a red flag. The risk framing that matters for you: those MAs are a long way below your $234.67 entry, so they're not useful as a near-term stop reference — that's why your stop is set off the recent breakout retest zone (~$231-232) instead, which is the right call. MAs matter more for judging the health of the broader trend than for picking today's stop level.

Also today: Golden cross / death cross — when the 50-day MA crosses above (golden) or below (death) the 200-day MA; a lagging but widely-watched trend-confirmation signal.
